## What's new

**Safer self-signed servers.** If your server uses a self-signed certificate,
`warren adduser` now prints a login command with `--fingerprint sha256:…`
instead of `--insecure`. warren then only talks to *your* server, so nobody in
between can grab your token. Print the fingerprint any time on the VPS with:

```sh
sudo -u warren warren fingerprint
```

Existing users can keep their token and just re-run their login command with
`--fingerprint …` added. `--insecure` still works, but `warren login` now warns
about it.

**Fixes**

- Reconnecting no longer fails with "tunnel limit reached" for users with a
  tunnel limit, e.g. after Wi-Fi drops or a laptop wakes up.
- Website tunnels refuse requests with oversized headers (431) instead of
  buffering them without limit.
- UDP tunnels can't get stuck on a client that stops reading.
- The server warns at startup if the control port has no TLS.

**Minecraft mod 0.2.0** understands `--fingerprint`: paste the whole login
command into the settings window as before and it's saved automatically.

> **Update your client too.** Login commands for self-signed servers now
> include `--fingerprint`, which warren 0.3.0 and older don't understand
> ("flag provided but not defined"). Run `warren update` first. On the VPS,
> `sudo warren update` also restarts the server.

0.4.0 uses the same protocol as earlier versions, so mixed versions keep
working together.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `warren-windows-amd64.exe` | Windows |
| `warren-darwin-arm64` | Mac with Apple chip (M1–M4) |
| `warren-darwin-amd64` | Mac with Intel chip |
| `warren-linux-amd64` | Linux / most VPSes |
| `warren-linux-arm64` | Linux on ARM (Oracle Ampere, Hetzner ARM, Raspberry Pi 64-bit) |
| `warren-mod-0.2.0+mc1.21.11.jar` | Minecraft mod (Fabric 1.21.11, needs Fabric API) |
| `setup.sh` | VPS setup wizard |
| `SHA256SUMS` | checksums (also used by `warren update`) |
